# Aubergine

> A local, browser-based canvas of terminal sessions for running several coding agents at once. It shows which agent is waiting for you, queues and schedules tasks, gives each agent its own working copy of a repository, and groups work in projects; sessions keep running when the browser closes. Everything runs on your own computer (127.0.0.1 only). Free and open source (MIT). Built for macOS; on Linux it has been run in containers only; on Windows it runs only inside WSL 2, not yet tried there. Needs tmux 3.2+, Node.js 22+. Install: npm install -g @meatgarden/aubergine.

## Start here

- [Landing page](https://thirstyeggplant.com/): what it does, install, FAQ
- [README](https://github.com/thirstyeggplant/aubergine/blob/main/README.md): full reference
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@meatgarden/aubergine): `npm install -g @meatgarden/aubergine`
- [Install script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thirstyeggplant/aubergine/main/install.sh): one-line installer that builds from the source (also needs pnpm), changes only ~/.aubergine and one link

## Pages

- [Claude Code in Aubergine](https://thirstyeggplant.com/claude/): what Aubergine does by itself for Claude Code, and where each thing is
- [Codex and ChatGPT in Aubergine](https://thirstyeggplant.com/chatgpt/): Codex runs in a terminal like any program; what it can report, and what is built only for Claude Code
- [Install](https://thirstyeggplant.com/install/): requirements, the installer, fixes
- [Install on Windows with WSL](https://thirstyeggplant.com/windows/): Aubergine inside WSL 2, used from a Windows browser; the Linux steps were run in a container, nothing on Windows yet
- [Run several coding agents at once](https://thirstyeggplant.com/run-multiple-coding-agents/)
- [Working copies](https://thirstyeggplant.com/working-copies/): an agent per checkout and branch
- [Keep your terminals after a restart](https://thirstyeggplant.com/keep-terminals-after-restart/): what closing the browser, restarting Aubergine and restarting the computer each keep, what is lost, and how to pick up where you were
- [Keep a process running after you close the terminal](https://thirstyeggplant.com/keep-process-running-after-closing-terminal/): nohup, disown, screen and tmux, and what Aubergine does: every terminal is a shell in tmux, so closing the browser or stopping Aubergine ends nothing; a restart of the computer does
- [Know when Claude Code is done or waiting for you](https://thirstyeggplant.com/claude-code-notifications/): working, waiting for you and finished from hooks Aubergine generates, the For you count, the next waiting key, notifications from the open page; no sound, nothing while no page is open
- [Resume a Claude Code conversation after a restart](https://thirstyeggplant.com/resume-claude-code-session/): claude --continue and --resume, Resume agent on the terminal a conversation ran in, past conversations in a folder, and what is read from Claude Code's own records
- [Find the right terminal when you have too many](https://thirstyeggplant.com/too-many-terminal-tabs/): the canvas, canvases and projects, one list of every terminal with its state in words, filters, tags, search of terminal output, and what was measured
- [tmux without learning tmux](https://thirstyeggplant.com/tmux-without-learning-tmux/): Aubergine runs tmux on its own socket with its own configuration: no prefix key, the wheel, copy and paste as in any terminal; your own tmux untouched; tmux 3.2 or newer needed
- [Check on your agents from your phone](https://thirstyeggplant.com/check-agents-from-your-phone/): reaching Aubergine from another device: HTTPS on the same computer, an address in the settings, devices paired with a code; run once on one Mac, not tried on a real phone
- [Customize terminal themes, colors, fonts and keys](https://thirstyeggplant.com/customize-terminal-themes/): ten color themes for the page, themes of your own as JSON files and an accent of your own, a theme for a project and for the terminals with a tag, a theme for each terminal, 35 colors set by hand in the settings file, a terminal's font and cursor, every key rebound, a settings file with a JSON Schema and a searchable list in Settings; what a program or an agent may change, and a theme an agent proposes for you to accept; and how VS Code, Zed, Obsidian, Hyper, WezTerm, tmux, kitty, Ghostty, Windows Terminal and iTerm2 document their own, read on 28 November 2026. templates for what a terminal's title and its row say; your own stylesheet (custom.css) with documented hooks; plugins, your own JavaScript in the page through a documented API, which run as you and are not sandboxed
- [The queue, For you and schedules](https://thirstyeggplant.com/queue-and-schedules/)
- [Tools for running several coding agents, compared](https://thirstyeggplant.com/compare/): Aubergine beside Conductor, Claude Squad, Vibe Kanban, cmux, Warp and Paradev (formerly Superset), from what each documents about itself on 26 November 2026; none of the others was run
- [Aubergine vs Conductor](https://thirstyeggplant.com/compare/conductor/): Conductor is a Mac app with chats, a diff viewer, pull requests and a cloud; Aubergine is a free, open-source local server showing plain terminals in a browser, kept running by tmux
- [Aubergine vs Claude Squad](https://thirstyeggplant.com/compare/claude-squad/): Claude Squad is a terminal program (TUI) that runs agents in tmux sessions and Git worktrees; Aubergine does the same from a browser page, with a canvas, waiting states, a queue and an API
- [Aubergine vs Vibe Kanban](https://thirstyeggplant.com/compare/vibe-kanban/): Vibe Kanban is a kanban board of issues that starts coding agents in Git worktrees and reviews their diffs; Aubergine is a canvas of plain terminals with a queue; both are local, open source and shown in a browser
- [Aubergine vs cmux](https://thirstyeggplant.com/compare/cmux/): cmux is a native macOS terminal app with a sidebar, panes and notifications for coding agents; Aubergine is a browser canvas of terminals kept running by tmux, with working copies, a queue and an HTTP API
- [Aubergine vs Warp](https://thirstyeggplant.com/compare/warp/): Warp is a desktop terminal for macOS, Windows and Linux with its own agent, plans and cloud agents; Aubergine calls no model and has no account, and runs your own agents in terminals on a canvas, kept running by tmux
- [Aubergine vs Paradev](https://thirstyeggplant.com/compare/paradev/): Paradev (formerly Superset) is an open-source desktop app with a worktree per task, a diff viewer, phone apps and paid plans; Aubergine is a free local server showing plain terminals on a canvas in a browser, with no account
- [Security and privacy](https://thirstyeggplant.com/security/): what is and is not protected
- [Roadmap](https://thirstyeggplant.com/roadmap/): planned, not built
- [FAQ](https://thirstyeggplant.com/faq/)

- [Guide for agents](https://github.com/thirstyeggplant/aubergine/blob/main/docs/for-agents.md)
- [API reference](https://github.com/thirstyeggplant/aubergine/blob/main/docs/api.md)

## Planned, not built yet

- Teams and connections: Multiplayer; Chat interface; Tickets and pull requests; Watches, webhooks and triage; Shared skills and a marketplace; Memory for people and rooms; Admin controls for models, sharing and strictness; A self-hosted team server; Sign-in for teams (SSO and MFA); Usage limits per person, token or agent; Read-only reports to share without sharing terminals; A phone view of the “For you” list; Reviewed connectors to company tools; More chat apps; Small internal web apps published to chosen people.
- Cloud: Sandboxed agents in the cloud; A pool of agents; Ready-made environments; Long, multi-phase work; One-command cloud deploy; Work you can see; MCP over HTTP, for agents on other machines; Tested Linux support; Shell integration beyond zsh.
- Control: Approval modes; Command policy and screening; Risk levels per repository; A full audit trail; Undo an agent's work; Admin controls; Model choice per terminal, task or schedule.
- Quality: Quality gates; Pull request review; Browser-driven testing; Plan before build; Task recipes; Outcome metrics; Incident write-ups: an agent investigates and drafts a postmortem.
- Make it yours: Other people's plugins: a sandboxed mode for a plugin someone else wrote, and installing one through the review screen (your own plugins, which run in the page as you, are built).
- Everywhere: Published SDK; Editor extension; Desktop app; Windows support (on Windows itself, not through WSL).

None of this exists today. Everything runs on one computer.
